rows.Conditions and triggers: This command MUST be issued by a node when the barrier has finished a transition (e.g. from Open to Close) and reached a final state
This command MUST be issued when a subsystem state has changed.
This command MUST be issued periodically to report the current battery level. The frequency is up to the implementation

This command MUST be issued by a node when its battery becomes low and the end user needs to reload or replace the battery. 
The Battery Level field MUST be set to 0xFF to indicate a low battery warning.
This command MUST be issued when the binary switch value has changed (and reached a final state)
This command MUST be issued by a node when a user actuated a Scene Notification button/method on the supporting node.
This command MUST be issued by a node when its Central Scene Configuration has changed.
This command MUST be issued when the clock setting has been modified.
This command MUST be issued when a color component level has changed.
This command MUST be issued by a node when it has completed a lock/unlock operation initiated locally.
This command MUST be issued by when the Door Lock configuration has changed.
This command MUST be issued by a node when it has been locally or manually reset to factory default.
This command MUST be issued by a node when a user input has exceeded key cache size or key cache timeout.
This command MUST be issued when a system error has occured.
This command SHOULD be issued when an indicator property has changed.

This command MUST be issued periodically to report the current Meter reading.
The sending frequency is up to the implementation. It is RECOMMENDED to implement a minimum reporting interval (for example, every 70 minutes) and send additional reports when a measurement variation occurred
A node supporting multiple meter types MUST advertise readings for all of the supported types via the Lifeline Group. Each meter type MAY have a different timing mechanism for reporting its readings.

This command MUST be issued periodically to report the current Multilevel sensor reading.
The sending frequency is up to the implementation. It is RECOMMENDED to implement a minimum reporting interval (for example, every 70 minutes) and send additional reports when a measurement variation occurred.
A node supporting multiple sensor types MUST advertise readings for all of the supported types via the Lifeline Group. Each sensor type MAY have a different timing mechanism for reporting its readings.
This command MUST be issued when the multilevel switch value has changed (and reached a final state)
This command MUST be issued by Push nodes every time a new event is detected or when a state variable has changed state.
This command MUST be issued when volume or default tone has changed.
This command MUST be issued when a tone has started playing.
This command MUST be issued when the Thermostat Mode has changed.
This command MUST be issued when the Thermostat Setback has changed.
This command MUST be issued when the Thermostat Setpoint setting has changed.
This command MUST be issued when a User Code record is modified.
This command MUST be issued when the Keypad Mode has been modified.
This command MUST be issued when the Master Code has been modified.
This command MUST be issued when a User Code record with user identifier > 255 has been modified.
This command MUST be issued when a Parameter ID has changed value.
